FAQ

## Questions, answered
Can’t find what you need? Ask us directly
What is continuous penetration testing?
Instead of one pentest a year, your application is attacked continuously: every week and every time you release new code. TensorShield’s AI agents do the testing, a senior expert verifies what they find, and you always have recent, signed evidence for auditors and customers.
Why “offense is the best defense”?
Attackers already use automation and AI to probe new code within hours of release. The only way to stay ahead is to attack your own systems first, continuously, and fix what you find before anyone else can use it.
How is this different from a vulnerability scanner?
Scanners match known patterns and report possibilities, often with many false alarms. Our agents log in as real users, chain steps together and prove what is actually exploitable, and a human expert confirms every serious finding. Auditors treat the result as a pentest, not a scan.
Will my SOC 2 or ISO 27001 auditor accept it?
Continuous plans include a signed yearly VAPT report built around what auditors check: scope, methodology, proof, retest and a named signer, plus quarterly evidence reports. The final call is always your auditor’s, so we’re happy to walk them through our approach before your audit.
What if I only need a one-time pentest report?
We offer that too: the Audit-Ready Pentest is ₹99,999 / $2,990 per app, with a signed report in 5–7 business days. Continuous includes that yearly pentest and keeps testing every release after it.

## Offense is the best defense. Start today.

URL: https://tensorshield.vercel.app/platform
Title: How It Works: Continuous AI Pentesting | TensorShield
Summary: How TensorShield tests web apps and APIs continuously: discovery, multi-role testing, AI exploitation, proof and expert verification on every release.
How it works

# An AI red team that never clocks out, with a human who signs off.
TensorShield combines deterministic security tooling, autonomous AI agents and experienced engineers into one continuous pipeline for your external web applications and APIs.
In shortWe discover your attack surface, log in as every role, attack like a skilled adversary, keep only findings we can prove, have a human verify the serious ones, and repeat on a schedule and on every deploy.
01

### Discover
Give us your app’s URL: we check DNS, technologies, login pages and published API specs, and propose the scope for you to approve. Nothing is tested until it is in scope.
02

### Authenticate
We test as each role you provide, with dedicated test accounts stored encrypted and checked before every run. Password and token logins are automated; MFA and SSO flows are tested by our engineers.
03

### Map
Authenticated crawling plus your OpenAPI or Postman specs map pages, endpoints and parameters.
04

### Attack
Deterministic tools cover breadth; AI agents go deep: multi-role access control, chained requests, business-logic probes.
05

### Prove
A finding exists only if it reproduces. Where possible it is proven by a deterministic check (an out-of-band callback, another user’s canary in a response), with hashed request and response evidence.
06

### Verify
A senior engineer reproduces every Critical and High, confirms impact and severity, and writes remediation guidance your team can act on.
Cadence

## Tested on a schedule. And on every change.
Continuous doesn’t mean noisy. We baseline your application, then focus each run on what changed, so you hear about new risk in hours and never about the same issue twice.

### On a schedule
Weekly, monthly or quarterly authenticated testing of every app, including multi-role access control.

### On every deploy
A signed webhook from GitHub or any CI pipeline triggers a quick run on what just shipped.

### When you fix
Mention a finding ID in a commit or pull request and its proof is replayed automatically.

### When a new exploit appears
A newly exploited CVE that matches your technology stack triggers a targeted check.
Coverage

## OWASP API Security Top 10, tested end to end.
Alongside the OWASP Top 10:2025 and the OWASP Web Security Testing Guide, here is how each API risk is covered.
Risk | How TensorShield tests it |
API1 · Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) | Multi-role request replay, proven with per-account canary values |
API2 · Broken Authentication | Login, reset and token handling; JWT weaknesses (MFA and SSO by our engineers) |
API3 · Broken Object Property Level Authorization | Mass assignment and excessive data exposure checks |
API4 · Unrestricted Resource Consumption | Safe, rate-limited checks for missing limits (no load testing) |
API5 · Broken Function Level Authorization | Privileged functions replayed as lower-privilege roles |
API6 · Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows | Agent-driven abuse of sign-up, checkout and invite flows |
API7 · Server-Side Request Forgery | Out-of-band callback verification on URL-handling parameters |
API8 · Security Misconfiguration | Headers, CORS, TLS, verbose errors, exposed debug endpoints |
API9 · Improper Inventory Management | Deprecated and undocumented endpoints reported when found during testing |
API10 · Unsafe Consumption of APIs | Injection through third-party data and webhook handlers |
Business-logic flaws, complex MFA/SSO flows and race conditions are assessed by a senior expert in every Audit-Ready Pentest.
Finding lifecycle

## From proof to closed, with receipts.
Every state change is timestamped, which is exactly the evidence an auditor samples for remediation and retest.
New
Proven and reproduced
Validated
Human-verified, ticket opened
Fixed
You request a retest or merge the fix
Retest passed
PoC replayed, closed with evidence
Onboarding

## Live in days, not weeks.
There is nothing to install. Here is everything we need from you to start testing.Book a free call
- A signed authorisation letter and rules of engagement (we provide the templates)
- In-scope domains, API base URLs and any out-of-scope paths
- OpenAPI / Swagger or a Postman collection (a GraphQL schema or HAR walkthrough helps our engineers)
- Two test accounts per user role (two tenants for multi-tenant apps)
- Our static egress IPs allow-listed on your WAF and rate limiter
- A security contact and an emergency phone number
- Optional: a GitHub or CI deploy webhook, and who should receive email alerts
FAQ

## Platform questions
Can’t find what you need? Ask us directly
Do I need to install anything?
No. For external web apps and APIs, testing runs from our infrastructure against your internet-facing assets. You allow-list our static IPs, give us test accounts and API specs, and we do the rest.
How do you avoid testing things we did not authorise?
Your approved scope is compiled into a network-level allow-list for each run’s isolated sandbox. Anything outside it is blocked and logged, regardless of what an AI agent decides. Newly discovered assets are only reported, and never tested until you approve them.
How is this different from DAST tools?
DAST tools crawl and match known patterns, usually as a single user. TensorShield tests as multiple roles, reasons about what each response means, chains steps together and proves exploitability, then a human verifies the result. That is how it finds access-control and logic flaws that scanners miss.
What happens when we fix something?
Request a retest in the portal, or mention the finding ID in your commit or pull request. We replay the proof through the same guardrails; if it no longer reproduces and the route was reached, the finding closes with retest evidence. On Audit-Ready engagements an engineer confirms the closure and issues a retest letter.
Can you test staging instead of production?
Yes, and for many teams that is the best choice. We recommend a staging environment that mirrors production, with production covered by safe, non-intrusive checks.

FAQ

## Pricing questions
Can’t find what you need? Ask us directly
What counts as one app?
One web application plus the APIs it uses, for example app.yourcompany.com and api.yourcompany.com. A separate product or a separate customer-facing portal counts as another app. We confirm this on the call before you pay anything.
Are there any extra costs?
No. The price includes testing, the report, the signed attestation letter and retests. Indian customers pay 18% GST on top. Customers outside India are billed in USD.
Is the Continuous plan worth it over a one-time pentest?
Continuous costs ₹1,99,990 / $3,990 a year for up to 3 apps and already includes your yearly pentest. If you ship often, it keeps you audit-ready all year and catches new issues within days instead of at next year’s test.
Do you offer discounts for early-stage startups?
Yes. Tell us your stage on the call. We also run a small founding-customer programme with a discount in exchange for feedback.
What if we need a more in-depth or specialised test?
Tell us on the call. Business-logic-heavy apps, many user roles or unusual stacks can need extra expert time, and we will quote it upfront before any work starts.

FAQ

## Startups: common questions
Can’t find what you need? Ask us directly
We just need one report for a customer. Can we start there?
Yes. The Audit-Ready Pentest is a one-time, fixed-price test with a signed report in 5–7 business days. Many startups upgrade to Continuous after their first audit.
Do we need a SOC 2 before a pentest?
No. Many teams run the pentest first because it surfaces issues to fix before the audit, and the report becomes evidence once the audit starts.
How much engineering time does it take?
About an hour to set up test accounts and share your API docs. After that, your team only sees verified issues with clear fixes.
Is it safe to test our production app?
Yes. Testing is limited to what you authorise, nothing destructive runs, and you can stop us at any time. Many startups use a staging copy instead.

FAQ

## Fintech: common questions
Can’t find what you need? Ask us directly
Are you CERT-In empanelled for RBI or SEBI audits?
Not yet. Where a regulator requires a CERT-In empanelled auditor, use one for that audit. TensorShield runs alongside it, testing every release so you stay secure between audits.
Does this cover PCI DSS penetration testing?
PCI DSS 11.4 requires a qualified, independent, human-led test. Our continuous testing helps you find and fix issues early, but use a PCI-qualified tester for the formal requirement.
Will testing create real transactions?
No. We test in staging or sandbox environments wherever possible and never execute real payments or transfers.
Can you test our mobile app’s APIs?
Yes. We test the APIs your mobile apps call, which is where most fintech vulnerabilities live.

FAQ

## Healthtech: common questions
Can’t find what you need? Ask us directly
Does HIPAA require a penetration test?
HIPAA requires regular risk analysis and evaluation of your technical safeguards. A pentest is not yet explicitly mandated, but it is the most common evidence hospitals and auditors expect.
Will you access real patient data?
We test with dedicated test accounts and data wherever possible. If a flaw exposes real data, we stop at the minimum proof needed and never extract it.
Can you sign a BAA or DPA?
We sign data processing agreements, and can discuss a BAA for US customers on the call.
Do you test mobile health apps?
We test the APIs your mobile apps use, which is where patient data is exposed in most cases.

FAQ

## SOC 2 pentest questions
Can’t find what you need? Ask us directly
Does SOC 2 require a penetration test?
SOC 2 does not list a pentest as a strict requirement, but in practice most auditors expect an annual third-party pentest (it supports criteria CC4.1 and CC7.1), and enterprise customers ask for one. If your SOC 2 system description or customer contracts mention pentesting, it becomes required.
When should we do the pentest for SOC 2?
For SOC 2 Type I, a test within the past 12 months is usually enough. For Type II, the test, your fixes and the retest should all happen inside your observation period, so start at least 8–10 weeks before it ends.
How much does a SOC 2 penetration test cost?
Traditional firms typically charge $5,000–25,000. TensorShield’s Audit-Ready Pentest is a fixed $2,990 (₹99,999 + GST in India) per app, including the report, attestation letter and a retest.
Will my auditor accept your report?
Our reports include everything auditors check for: scope, methodology, proof, retest and a named signer. The final decision is always your auditor’s, so we’re happy to walk them through our approach before your audit.
Is an automated scan enough for SOC 2?
Usually not. Many auditors treat scanner output as vulnerability scanning, not a penetration test. Every TensorShield report includes expert-verified findings with proof, which is what makes it a pentest.

FAQ

## ISO 27001 pentest questions
Can’t find what you need? Ask us directly
Does ISO 27001 require penetration testing?
ISO 27001:2022 doesn’t explicitly require a pentest, but it requires you to find and fix technical vulnerabilities (Annex A 8.8) and to test security (8.29). A pentest report is the most common and convincing evidence auditors look for.
How often should we pentest for ISO 27001?
At least once a year, in line with your surveillance audits, and after major changes to your application.
How much does an ISO 27001 pentest cost?
TensorShield’s Audit-Ready Pentest is a fixed $2,990 (₹99,999 + GST in India) per app, including the report, attestation letter and a retest.
What does the report include?
What we tested and when, our methodology, every finding with proof and how to fix it, the Annex A controls it supports, retest results and a signed attestation letter.

FAQ

## VAPT in India: common questions
Can’t find what you need? Ask us directly
What is VAPT?
VAPT stands for Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing. We look for security weaknesses in your web application and APIs, then safely try to exploit them to prove which ones are real. You get a report with each issue, its risk and how to fix it.
How much does VAPT cost in India?
Web application VAPT in India usually costs between ₹40,000 and ₹1,50,000 per application. TensorShield charges a fixed ₹99,999 per app (plus GST), which includes expert verification, a SOC 2 and ISO 27001-ready report, a signed attestation letter and a free retest.
Do I get a VAPT certificate?
Yes. You get a signed attestation letter (often called a VAPT certificate) that summarises what was tested, when, and the result. After you fix the issues, we retest and issue an updated letter.
Is TensorShield CERT-In empanelled?
Not yet. If you are regulated by RBI, SEBI, IRDAI or a government body that specifically requires a CERT-In empanelled auditor, you will need an empanelled firm for that audit. For SOC 2, ISO 27001, customer reviews and due diligence, CERT-In empanelment is not required.
Do you provide a GST invoice?
Yes. Indian customers receive a GST invoice in INR. Prices on this page exclude 18% GST.

URL: https://tensorshield.vercel.app/trust
Title: Trust & Safety: Guardrails and AI Disclosure | TensorShield
Summary: How TensorShield keeps AI pentesting safe: network-enforced scope, non-destructive tests, kill switch, vaulted credentials, audit logs and full AI disclosure.
Trust & safety

# Powerful enough to find real bugs. Controlled enough to trust.
Letting an AI attack your systems should make you ask hard questions. Here are our answers: what we test, how we limit it, how we use AI, and who is accountable.

### Network-enforced scope
Every run executes in its own isolated sandbox whose only route out is a scope gateway. It allows only the hosts in your approved scope, refuses private and cloud-metadata addresses, and logs every allowed and blocked request.

### Safe testing tiers
Default checks are non-destructive, and tests that could modify data or exhaust resources are excluded unless you opt in, in writing. Excluded paths are blocked at the network for plain HTTP; over HTTPS the agent is instructed to avoid them and an engineer reviews anything that touches them.

### Rate limits & testing windows
Per-host request limits and optional time windows keep load predictable. We never run denial-of-service tests.

### Kill switch
Stop any run from the portal or by calling us: traffic is cut at the network first, within seconds. A run that keeps trying out-of-scope targets is stopped automatically.

### Static, published egress IPs
Allow-list them on your WAF. We do not attempt to bypass or evade your defensive controls.

### Credentials handled with care
Test credentials are encrypted in a vault, released only to the run that needs them and masked in every log and report. The AI agent uses them to log in, so we ask for dedicated, low-privilege test accounts.

### Tamper-evident audit trail
Every approval, sign-off and status change is kept in a hash-chained log, and every request a run makes is logged by the scope gateway. Its hash is included in your evidence pack.

### Human approval gates
New assets are reported, never tested, until you approve adding them to scope, and a TensorShield engineer approves every scope change and every run.

### Data retention & deletion
Engagement data is retained only as long as your contract requires, then deleted, with written confirmation on request.
Methodology

## How we test
Our testing follows established, publicly documented methodologies so that auditors and your security team can understand and verify our approach:
- OWASP Web Security Testing Guide (WSTG) for web application test cases
- OWASP Top 10:2025 and OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023) for risk categorisation
- OWASP ASVS 5.0 as a verification reference
- PTES and NIST SP 800-115 for engagement phases, from pre-engagement to reporting
- CVSS 3.1 and 4.0 for severity, computed from the vector, never estimated by an AI
- CWE identifiers for every finding, validated against MITRE’s list
A finding is reported only if it is reproducible and supported by captured evidence. Every Critical and High is reproduced by a human before it is delivered.

## AI disclosure
We believe you have a right to know exactly how AI is involved in testing your systems.
- What AI does: plans and executes test steps, analyses responses, attempts exploitation within scope, de-duplicates results and drafts report text.
- What humans do: agree scope and rules of engagement, verify serious findings, confirm severity, review every report, sign attestation letters, and perform expert-led testing in every Audit-Ready Pentest.
- Models: we use large language models from providers that do not store your data or train on it by default, processed in India for Indian customers where the provider supports it. The exact model, provider and region are named in your authorisation letter.
- Training: your data is never used to train or fine-tune models.
- Sub-processors: every infrastructure and model provider that may process engagement data is named in your authorisation letter and data processing agreement before testing begins.

## Authorised testing only
We only test assets that the customer owns or is authorised to test, under a signed authorisation letter and rules of engagement. We do not test third-party services (for example your SaaS vendors or cloud provider control planes) without that provider’s permission, and we follow the published penetration testing policies of major cloud providers.

## Reporting a vulnerability in TensorShield
If you believe you have found a security issue in our website or services, please see our responsible disclosure policy or email tensorshield@gmail.com.

# Security that moves as fast as you ship.
TensorShield exists to close the gap between how often software changes and how often it gets tested, without sacrificing the rigour that auditors, customers and security leaders depend on.

## Ashish Mishra
Founder, TensorShield
15+ years in cybersecurity Google Intel View LinkedIn profile
Founder

### More than fifteen years defending systems at global scale, at Google and Intel.
Ashish Mishra has spent over 15 years in cybersecurity, building and securing systems at some of the world’s most demanding engineering organisations, including Google and Intel. That experience shaped a simple conviction: the attackers are already automated, and the defence has to be too.
Most teams still buy security testing the way they did a decade ago: one engagement a year, a PDF weeks later, and a long gap until the next one. Meanwhile they ship every day. TensorShield combines AI agents that test continuously with the judgment of experienced engineers, so every release is tested and every report stands up to an auditor.
Ashish leads TensorShield’s methodology, quality standards and sign-off, and works directly with every early customer.
What we believe

## Four principles we won’t trade away.

### Proof over noise
If we can’t demonstrate it, we don’t report it. Every finding ships with a working proof of concept and the evidence behind it.

### Humans stay accountable
AI tests relentlessly. A named, experienced engineer verifies what matters and signs what goes to your auditor.

### Guardrails are infrastructure
Scope, rate limits and kill switches are enforced in the network, not left to a model’s judgment.

### Radical transparency
We disclose how we use AI, which providers process data, and exactly what was tested, when and how.
Our mission
Give every software team, from a five-person startup to a scaling enterprise, the continuous, provable security testing that used to be reserved for companies with a red team.
